newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-Portugal prices EDP sale aggressively.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Portugal prices EDP sale aggressively.

text.p: Portugal on Thursday set a price of 1,750-2,250 escudos ($1.02-1.32) per share for the partial privatisation of state electricity concern EDP, the biggest state sale yet carried out in the country.
The privatisation should raise up to 400 billion escudos, if the state floats between 20 and 30 percent of the company, although the exact percentage to be sold will be set early next month.
Government officials have said that it sees between 20 and 30 percent as a reasonable target but it is ready to float even more if demand is there.
Analysts expected strong demand for the electricity concern, which increased its net profit last year by 22 percent to 81 billion escudos.
"EDP meets all the requirements to become a great company once it is launched on the bourse," said Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco.

The privatisation comes at a favourable moment for the Lisbon bourse which has gained some 30 percent so far this year, helped by news that one of the world's most watched stock rating agencies, the Morgan Stanley Capital International, plans to promote the market to developed from emerging.
The switch will automatically bring in cash from big international investment funds.
Portuguese banks, which have opened special savings accounts for investors to accumulate funds for buying EDP stocks, said there was already 180 billion escudos in the accounts.
"It certainly seems attractively priced," said one Lisbon analyst who asked not to be named.
Analysts said the flotation valued EDP at between 1.05 and 1.35 trillion escudos, below the 1.4-1.7 trillion price tag often estimated earlier by the press.
Some of the shares will be sold directly to foreign and institutional investors through a process of bookbuilding, with the remainder going to local investors.
Employees, small investors and emigrants will be offered a discount and there will be bonus shares for investors who hold the stock for more than a year.
The bookbuilding begins on May 26 with the Lisbon bourse session to decide pricing and allocations of stock set for June 16.
"It is an attractive and interesting price range," said analyst Joao Vermelho of Central de Investimentos.
Analysts said that by setting the range at slightly below market forecasts, the government was allowing room for the price to rise on its launch on the bourse.
"I have not the slightest doubt (that the operation) will be carried out at the top end of the range because the demand is going to be very high," said another analyst who asked not to be named.
"It is below the 2,100-2,600 escudos many had expected and should allow the stock to rise later," added another analyst.
